rewrites.summary: Bolu sits under the same intensifying national framework that binds every province of Türkiye; no province-specific ordinance, incident series or court decision concerning trans visitors was documented in this research pass, so the national picture below is the whole documented picture for Bolu. A leaked draft of the 11th Judicial Package (October 2025) would criminalise LGBT conduct and advocacy — up to three years for behaviour 'contrary to biological sex and general morality', up to four years for taking part in a same-sex engagement or marriage ceremony (the record's only marriage-related item, so a trans visitor travelling with a partner faces it directly) — and would raise the minimum age for gender-affirming care including surgery from 18 to 25 with mandatory permanent infertility, exposing providers to fines and up to seven years and patients to up to three years. The Kaos GL 2025 human-rights report finds hostility became explicit state policy in 2025, with senior officials' rhetoric and instructions to public institutions under a national family-policy banner ('Year of the Family') creating a climate that encouraged human-rights violations.
rewrites.tangentialFactors: Parent-nation policy turbulence: the October 2025 package is a leaked draft rather than enacted law — the rights-monitoring organisation Human Rights Watch called it one of the most alarming rollbacks of LGBT rights in decades — and 15 LGBT groups plus the Turkish Medical Association objected. The Kaos GL 2025 human-rights report's counts are country-wide figures — six right-to-life violations, three recorded as hate-motivated killings with trans people most affected, 89 torture or ill-treatment cases (up from 51) and 313 liberty violations, a roughly 2.5-fold increase — counted from media coverage because the state keeps no hate-crime statistics — presented as national practice rather than provincial choice, with no provincial breakdown for this province.
